dossier.public_summary: The dip appears only in two very deep events and disappears completely in some sectors, inconsistent with a planet on the target. A V-shaped dip, a ~30% secondary eclipse, and a large odd/even difference instead point to a grazing binary/blend blended into the aperture. The signal is not a planet.

reasons.why: Signal is carried almost entirely by two deep transits; chi2 549.9 on 16 dof shows extreme inconsistency. This is not a small measurement scatter but a few events driving the detection, typical of systematics/systematic blends rather than a stable planet.
reasons.value: share_of_top_3: 0.921, p_consistent: 9.33844323031878e-107, outliers: 2 events at 1684 ppm and 1717 ppm sigma 15.0 and 14.4

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor of ~500 between sectors and essentially vanishes in sectors 52 and 79. A planet on the target must be steady; changes_within_a_source with near-zero depth in some sectors and very deep in others positively favors a blend or a few corrupted events over a planet.
reasons.value: sectors p_constant: 8.957e-32 depth_change_pct: 514.5, SPOC 2-min p_constant: 2.103013635463789e-28, sectors: 53 depth 1699 +/-145 ppm vs 52 depth 11 +/-38 ppm, 79 depth 8 +/-33 ppm

reasons.why: Significant secondary eclipse at phase 0.6792 with depth ~30% of dip and phase offset 0.1792 from half-orbit, plus factor 1.5 odd/even difference and V-shaped (v_sigma 2.749, grazing b 0.981) shape. Together with variable depth this matches an eclipsing binary / diluted blend, not a small planet. Coincidence of a phase-curve chi2 16.07 and variability flag supports binary over planet.

reasons.why: Independent classifier trained on follow-up calls this as strongly planet-unlike, consistent with the inconsistency and secondary signals above.
